# Copilot instructions: ifc_tools

Header-only ROS 2 (lyrical) + OpenCV 4.10 utility package, C++20, for the `ifc` colcon workspace (this repo lives at `<ws>/src/ifc_tools`). First consumer is `horizon_detection`.

## Build / run
Run from the workspace root (two levels up), not this directory:

```bash
source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash
colcon build --packages-select ifc_tools
source install/setup.bash
ros2 run ifc_tools mosaic
```

`mosaic` also calls `render` from a 1 s wall timer so the window and FPS refresh when no frames arrive.

The tests are the headless CTests `ifc_tools_ring_buffer`, `ifc_tools_interpolator` and `ifc_tools_kalman_filter_1d` (`test/` mirrors `include/ifc_tools/`) (`colcon test --packages-select ifc_tools --ctest-args -R interpolator` runs one); there are no linters. Verify GUI/ROS code by building and running the example. The example needs a FlightGear publisher on `/flightgear/image` (`bgr8`, `SensorDataQoS`), the `compressed_image_transport` plugin, and a desktop. Warnings are enabled (`-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`); keep the build warning-free.

## Architecture
- Single `INTERFACE` CMake target `ifc_tools` (exported via `ament_export_targets`); all code is in headers under `include/ifc_tools/`, namespace `ifc_tools`, grouped by role: `common/` (`debug_viewer.hpp`, `performance_monitor.hpp`), `processing/` (`ring_buffer.hpp`, `interpolator.hpp`), `receiver/` (`buffered_receiver.hpp`, `image_receiver.hpp`), `filter/` and `msg/` (one header per ROS message, named after it in snake_case). New dependencies must be added to `CMakeLists.txt` (`find_package`, link, `ament_export_dependencies`) and `package.xml`.
- `examples/*.cpp` are built as executables and installed to `lib/ifc_tools`; register new ones in `CMakeLists.txt`.
- `ImageReceiver` (an `rclcpp::Node`): subscribes via `image_transport::create_subscription(*this, topic, cb, transport, rclcpp::SensorDataQoS())` (the `rclcpp::Node*` overload is deprecated). Converts with `cv_bridge::toCvShare(msg, "bgr8")` and calls a mutex-protected `std::function<void(const rclcpp::Time&, const cv::Mat&)>` set with `setCallback`. The `cv::Mat` is only valid during the callback; copy it to keep it.
- `DebugViewer(cv::Size, size_t rows, size_t cols)`: fixed-grid mosaic in one OpenCV window. `update(row, col, mat)` (zero-based) copies/letterboxes an image into a cell and counts a frame for that tile; `render(timestamp_us)` takes a monotonic `uint64_t` time in microseconds, recomputes each tile's FPS once per second, draws a green FPS HUD on a clone of the mosaic (the stored mosaic stays clean), then `imshow` + `pollKey`. Accepts 8-bit gray/BGR/BGRA only. Single-thread use (the callback thread).
- The horizon detector base currently stores an optional `DebugViewer`; its construction and use are not wired yet.
- `RingBuffer<T>(capacity)`: fixed-capacity FIFO that overwrites the oldest element when full. Storage for `capacity` elements is reserved in the constructor, so `push` never reallocates. Index 0 is the oldest; provides `front` (peek oldest), `back`, `popFront` (removes the oldest; throws `std::out_of_range` when empty), `operator[]`, a const forward iterator (`begin`/`end`) and `toVector`. Not thread-safe; callers lock. Tested by CTest `ifc_tools_ring_buffer` (`colcon build --packages-select ifc_tools --cmake-args -DBUILD_TESTING=ON && colcon test --packages-select ifc_tools`).
- `processing/interpolator.hpp`: `InterpolationMethod<T>` (pure virtual `interpolate(a, b, float alpha) -> T`, a classic abstract interface, not traits) with the default `Nearest<T>`; and `Interpolator<Container>`, a non-owning decorator (holds a const reference; binding a temporary is deleted) of any iterable container of elements `T` with a public `timestamp` member, sorted by ascending timestamp (the timestamp type is deduced from `T::timestamp`). The method interpolates whole elements. `interpolate(timestamp, method = Nearest<T>())` and `interpolate(ascending_timestamps, method = Nearest<T>())` return `std::optional<T>` (per query for the vector) using a forward-only bracket, with `timestamp` set to the query; outside the time range (before the first or after the last sample) they return `std::nullopt`. An empty container throws `std::out_of_range`. Use with CTAD: `ifc_tools::Interpolator(samples).interpolate(ts, method)`.
- `filter/kalman_filter_1d.hpp`: `KalmanFilter1D<T>(Parameters {dQdt, innov_gate_sd})`, a ROS-free scalar random-walk Kalman filter. `initialize(x, P)`; `predict(dt)` adds `dQdt·dt` to `P` (negative `dt` is ignored); `update(z, R)` rejects `z` when `|z − x|/√(P + R) > innov_gate_sd`, otherwise applies `K = P/(P + R)`; both return `false` when uninitialized or rejected (state unchanged). `initialized()`, `state()` → `{x, P}`. Units are the caller's.
- `MessageConverter<Message, Value>` (`receiver/buffered_receiver.hpp`; pure virtual `convert(message) -> std::optional<Value>`, where `Value` has a public `timestamp` member; empty rejects the message).
- `BufferedReceiver<Message, Value>(node_name, converter, capacity, topic, qos = SensorDataQoS)`: an `rclcpp::Node` (like `ImageReceiver`; add it to the executor) that converts each message and pushes it into a mutex-protected `RingBuffer<Value>`. It drops a sample whose timestamp equals the last one and clears the buffer (with a warning) when the timestamp goes backwards (simulation reset). `snapshot()` returns the buffer as a `std::vector<Value>` for computation off the callback; decorate it with `Interpolator`. `interpolateAndPrune(timestamp, method, keep = 0)` interpolates one timestamp under the lock (`std::nullopt` when empty or out of range) and on success drops all samples older than the earlier one used except the `keep` newest of them, for consumers moving forward in time.
- `msg/*.hpp`: per message a value struct (`timestamp` in ns), a `<Name>Receiver` alias of `BufferedReceiver` and a `<Name>Utils` `MessageConverter` (plus `InterpolationMethod` for PX4 messages). PX4 stamps use `timestamp_sample` µs→ns. `vehicle_attitude.hpp`: `VehicleAttitude {timestamp, Eigen::Quaterniond q}`, normalized, rejects zero/non-finite norm, slerp. `vehicle_local_position.hpp`: `VehicleLocalPosition {timestamp, Eigen::Vector3d position, velocity}` (NED; x, y NaN unless `xy_valid`, z unless `z_valid`, likewise velocity with `v_xy_valid`/`v_z_valid`), linear. `vehicle_global_position.hpp`: `VehicleGlobalPosition {timestamp, double latitude, longitude, float altitude_amsl}` (NaN unless `lat_lon_valid` / `alt_valid`), interpolated on the unit normal (n-vector) and converted back, so the antimeridian and poles are handled. `vehicle_angular_velocity.hpp`: `VehicleAngularVelocity {timestamp, Eigen::Vector3d omega}` (FRD body rad/s), linear. `features.hpp`: `Features {timestamp[2], Eigen::Matrix2d A, Eigen::Vector2d b}` from `ifc_msgs/Features` (`x₂ = A·x₁ + b`; rejects non-finite or non-increasing pairs). `horizon.hpp`: `Horizon {timestamp (image), theta, rho}` from `ifc_msgs/Horizon` (rejects `confidence <= 0` or non-finite), plus static `HorizonUtils::groundMask(size, theta, rho, margin_px)`, the 8-bit mask of the image below the horizon shifted down by `margin_px`.

## Conventions
- Brace-on-own-line (Allman) style, 4-space indent, `_`-prefixed private members (`_callback_mutex`), `#pragma once`.
